# Two-Key

Authorization layer for AI agents. A tool call runs only if a deterministic
policy VM and an independent LLM-judge quorum both approve. The gateway then
accepts a short-lived single-use capability token bound to the exact argument
bytes, and writes the decision to a signed Merkle ledger. The ledger is
AES-256-GCM. Its decryption key and witness key live outside the ledger
directory. The principal key cannot unwrap it.

Prototype. Not production crypto. Not FIPS validated. Algorithms are chosen so a later build can run on a validated module. Python >= 3.10.
Install from this repository: pip install -e ".[yaml,pq]".
Package version 0.1.6. Apache-2.0.

Entry points: docs/FIT.md, docs/COMPARISON.md, docs/THREAT_MODEL.md, README.md, docs/HOWTO.md, docs/SPEC_DRAFT.md, SECURITY.md.
CLI: python -m two_key. Offline demo: python -m two_key demo.
Tests: python -m unittest discover -s tests (447 tests, 3 skipped without SoftHSM, no network).

There is no MCP server in this release. capability-tokens are the tool-binding
mechanism. Do not treat GitHub topics as the API.
Monitored agents are optional and configured in examples/agents.yaml. They may be local or vendor-hosted (xAI, OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, Ollama). authorize_from_agent sends the constitution, then both paths still decide. The agent cannot execute a tool.
A missing ballot is not a yes. Path A is only as good as the structured action record it is given.
Scanner, PKI, Fabric, and HSM integrations in this repository are hooks. The tests use fakes, not live products.
